title: Evening Flock — Ask whether pointing a flight changes its place
summary: Try three questions about place and flight
lead: Pause the sky to make one deliberate change. These are steering experiments with eighty toy birds, not measurements of a real flock.

questions.title: Does pointing toward the center move a bird?
questions.prompt: Pause, open the current-flight tools and press Fly toward the sky center. Look at the places before taking an ordinary Step.
questions.answer: The press changes each moving bird’s velocity direction, keeping its current speed and place. Birds at rest and birds exactly at the center remain unchanged. A later ordinary beat moves the sky and applies the ordinary engine rules; the pointing press itself does not.

questions.title: Will a resting bird join that pointing gesture?
questions.prompt: Rest one side of the sky, then point the current flights toward the center. Compare the resting side with the moving side. Use Step back after trying it.
questions.answer: Not in the pointing press. A zero-speed bird remains exactly at rest. On a later ordinary beat, neighbor steering may change it again. Rest is a current condition, not a permanent category of bird.

questions.title: Is a new sky an Undo step?
questions.prompt: Keep a beat, then choose a starting sky and apply it. Compare that with changing the current flights.
questions.answer: Starting a sky replaces the eighty-bird arrangement and clears beat history. A current-flight edit instead saves one beat snapshot, so Step back restores the whole press. Starting conditions and interventions are different experiments.
